## 10. Garanties et limites formelles du jalon 1

Cette section décrit la portée vérifiée de l'exploration Lean ; les noms exacts des théorèmes et leur classement détaillé figurent dans l'**annexe non normative A**. L'exploration est rapportée comme ayant construit, sans avertissement, 607 théorèmes et 362 exemples, sans `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom`, `native_decide` ni `noncomputable` dans `formal/`, et avec `#print axioms` ne faisant apparaître au plus que `propext` et `Quot.sound`. Il s'agit de résultats **déclarés dans le rapport de passe 8**, non d'un audit indépendant du module source.

La propriété centrale est la préservation de `WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan ∧ ArenaInv` sur tous les états atteints depuis `S3.init statics`, **sous `DDSound(K)`**. Des contre-exemples confirment que la même conclusion serait fausse si l'on supprimait certaines hypothèses structurelles ou le contrat de disjonction.

Les preuves portent sur les **accès du noyau abstrait séquentiel**. Elles n'établissent ni l'absence générale de fuites et de blocages, ni la terminaison, ni les propriétés de la concurrence, ni la correction du compilateur ou de la traduction mémoire MM-02. Les garanties différées ne sont pas promises par la présente section.

## 11. Cas d'épreuve et matériel non normatif

Les cas d'épreuve constituent des témoins de validation d'un modèle ; ils ne donnent pas, par leur seule présence, autorité à des règles qui contrediraient les sections 1–9. Les cas en annexe B reprennent des verdicts effectivement décrits dans les rapports Lean. Les corpus adversariaux complets MM2-H, MM3-H et MM23-H sont **réservés au jalon 3**, sans présumer de verdicts encore absents des sources disponibles.

## 12. Hors périmètre, décisions différées et critères de validation

Cette section ne fixe pas la syntaxe des autorités ou des valeurs non échappantes, les annotations de signatures, la généricité, la suspension asynchrone, les destructeurs, les règles complètes de `defer`, la libération automatique de toutes les ressources, le protocole des handles persistants, les graphes à résolution contrôlée, la politique complète des globales mutables, la sémantique concurrente ni le lowering final des accès bruts.

| Sujet différé | Destination retenue |
|---|---|
| Raffinement MM-03 → MM-02 (R1, R2, R4, R6), `DDSound` réel, adresses, allocation, désallocation, provenance, épinglage, initialisation, `store` de pointeur, arènes, justification mémoire de `noalias` | **Jalon 2 de la Spec 1** |
| Prévention locale de l’auto-blocage par `transfer` et `issue` (option 2) | **Retenue** dans O4/O18 ; l’acyclicité globale (`NoLock`, option 3) n’est pas adoptée. H49 et H51 restent des limites d’ergonomie documentées ; les liens persistants passent par des handles. |
| Corpus adversariaux MM3-H et MM23-H | **Jalon 3 achevé**, sous les écarts connus explicités dans son rapport ; MM2-H doit encore être exécuté contre la reconstruction de référence. Les cas concurrents dépendants sont à rouvrir après la Spec 2. |
| Protection forte sur toute la durée d'invocation (`Reach`, `lineage`, `derivedIn`, G1', A3 strict) | **Spec 3 — Contrôle de flux** |
| Traduction bas niveau des hypothèses de non-aliasing | **Spec 13 — Architecture du compilateur** |
| Concurrence, atomiques, synchronisation, transférabilité et partageabilité entre threads | **Spec 2 — Modèle de concurrence** |
| `defer` et discipline générale des obligations de libération | **Spec 3 et spécification appropriée des ressources** |

Les jalons 1–3 sont clos dans les limites documentées de leurs rapports. La présente v0.4 incorpore seulement les décisions expressément retenues à leur issue. Le modèle exploratoire doit être reconstruit après validation du document normatif assemblé ; cette reconstruction doit vérifier les écarts et obligations des registres, sans correction silencieuse du texte. La clôture des jalons ne vaut pas gel de la Spec 1 complète.

# Annexe A — Statut des preuves Lean (non normative)

_Source : `MM03_v0.1_p8.md`, section (q).1. Les noms de théorèmes sont des références au module exploratoire, pas des axiomes normatifs._

## A.1 — Invariants sur les états atteints

| Garantie | Conditions de validité | Théorèmes rapportés |
|---|---|---|
| `WF3` ; I1, I2, I3, I4 ; `AnchorOrder`, `NoDangling` | `Reachable k statics s` et `DDSound k` | `reachable_invariants`, `reachable_access_invariant_ext` |
| `AnchorOrderHeld` | mêmes conditions | `reachable_anchorOrderHeld` |
| `NoOrphan` | mêmes conditions | `reachable_no_orphan`, `reachable_rootLive` |
| `ArenaInv` et stockage utilisable des arènes vivantes | mêmes conditions | `reachable_access_invariant_ext`, `live_arena_storage_usable` |
| Aucune lecture sûre après invalidation, côté MM-03 | mêmes conditions | `reachable_no_dangling`, `exitFrame_no_dangling_reachable` |

## A.2 — Propriétés de pas et de l'état initial

| Garantie | Hypothèses pertinentes | Théorèmes rapportés |
|---|---|---|
| Préservation de l'exclusivité par dérivation et séparation | I1 ; `DDSound`/`Inv3base` pour `split` | `derive_preserves_exclusivity`, `split_preserves_exclusivity_underDD`, `effective_exclusive`, `write3_exclusive` |

| Émissions d'arène disjointes, conservation des blocs, rejet du reset vivant et réutilisation sûre | `WF3`, `Inv3base`, `ArenaInv` | `arena_issue_preserves_disjointness`, `arena_issue_keeps_earlier_blocks`, `arena_reset_rejects_live_issued`, `arena_reuse_safe` |
| Déplacement des autorités et de la possession vers les parties correspondantes | `WF3` pour la correspondance de parties | `transfer_to_corresponding_parts`, `transfer_moves_ownership`, `transfer_no_duplicate_authority` |
| Paramètres à l'entrée et exclusivité effective tant que le paramètre est actif | `WF3`, `Inv3base` / I1 | `enter_params_protected`, `call_params_effective_protected` |

| Initialisation déclarée dans l'état initial | aucune | `init_statics` |
| Une seule feuille écrite par `store`, destination encore accessible | précondition `StorePre` | `store_writes_one_leaf`, `store_keeps_target_reachable` |
| Source rendue `Moved`, aucune autorité dupliquée | pas `transfer` `ok` | `transfer_invalidates_source`, `transfer_no_duplicate_authority` |
| `reset` refuse les dépendances ou dérivées encore vivantes | préconditions correspondantes | `arena_reset_rejects_live_dependents` |
| Déterminisme des relations d'opérations | relations respectives | famille `*_det` |

## A.3 — Garanties non prouvées par le jalon 1

La forme forte de F6 (`call_protects_params_safe`) est réfutée par des états atteints, et non remplacée par un théorème silencieusement affaibli. L'absence de `NoLock` est compatible avec les invariants prouvés, mais ne garantit pas l'absence d'autorités détenues devenues inexerçables. Sans `DDSound`, le témoin `split_unsound_without_DD` réfute l'exclusivité globale. Hors de `WF3`, certains transferts peuvent faire tomber `Inv3` : ces états ne sont pas atteints dans le cadre du théorème principal. Le jalon 1 n'a pas encore de théorème autonome reliant tous les constructeurs `Reachable` à `Step` ni de théorème historique global sur chaque feuille `Init` atteinte : ces deux lemmes sont prévus pour la reconstruction de référence.

# Annexe B — Cas d'épreuve constatés (non normative)

# Annexe F — Registre de reconstruction de référence (non normatif)

La reconstruction de référence doit repartir du texte **validé**, et non des approximations du brouillon. Les éléments suivants ne sont pas tous prouvés à ce stade :

1. **Six écarts du brouillon MM-03** (`MM23_v0.1.md`, section (f)) : (i) feuilles lues/écrites utilisables, (ii) empreintes composées uniquement de feuilles, (iii) `alloc` créant une racine unique, (iv) marques de mort transitives après `free` et `endUse`, (v) `RootLive`/`RootHeld`, (vi) bonne fondation des chaînes de possession.
2. **Locaux de `enterFrame`** : rendre explicite que les locaux créés par l'opération sont possédés directement par le cadre ; une forme de local ayant pour propriétaire un autre local n'est pas une forme de `enterFrame` admise.
3. **Jalon 2 — décisions 1 à 4** : (i) disjonction déclarée des **feuilles**, à justifier par la bibliothèque, puis disjonction des plages d'octets sous `LayoutWF` ; (ii) adresse/provenance d'une région vide = base/allocation de son ancre effective ; (iii) pour une région non vide, adresse minimale des feuilles de taille non nulle, sans confondre pointeur et représentation d'une région non contiguë ; (iv) feuille recevant une référence de taille exactement adaptée au pointeur et `decode` lisant uniquement ces octets (obligations Specs 4/11).
4. **Jalon 2 — autres points** : `SameSizeAlong` demeure à la Spec 4, `Repr` inclut `MM02.WF`, `freeSound_derived` et fournisseur conservé, simulation conditionnelle à paramètres fixés ; ne pas présenter le théorème de simulation comme une validation autonome de tous les contenus binaires.
5. **Induction d'initialisation** : toute feuille `Init` atteinte l'était à l'état initial ou provient d'une écriture autorisée, d'un transfert légal ou d'une émission écrivant explicitement sa destination. **Correspondance `Step` / `Reachable`** : démontrer la liaison des constructeurs et transitions opérationnelles générales, non seulement les cas isolés.
6. **Reconstruction `HandlePool`** : réénoncer et prouver `PoolInv` corrigé ; prouver l'effet de `freeSlot` sous `MetaRight`, notamment lorsque seul `writeShared` autorise la mutation des métadonnées ; vérifier `resolveMany Observe`, les deux registres et le stockage `Uninit` de `newPool` ; vérifier la propriété d'exclusivité à travers toutes les opérations du noyau.
7. **Corpus MM2-H** : exécuter les 17 identifiants d'origine (H13 scindé en H13a/H13b, donc 18 scénarios) sur la reconstruction de référence, et non sur le vieux brouillon ; conserver les cas de formation d'adresse et reconstruction de pointeur non tranchés par MM-02.G comme obligations, sans les décréter réussis.
8. **MM23-H15/H16** : enregistrer et corriger les écarts connus de pointeurs vides/ordre des feuilles, sans les présenter comme des preuves déjà acquises.
9. **Option 2 `NoLock`** : reconstruire et vérifier la nouvelle précondition locale de O4 et O18 ; H49 et H51 restent des limites d'ergonomie (cycles d'autorités, non UB) ; l'option 3 globale n'est pas adoptée.
10. **Appels** : enregistrer la primitive de `sink` à l'entrée d'appel et les conditions du ré-emprunt H01 pour la Spec 3, sans les introduire silencieusement dans les transitions courantes de MM-03.

La reconstruction utilisera un journal de traçabilité clause → définition → théorème → cas, et distinguera l'ensemble des garanties effectivement prouvées des conditions de programme bien typé, d'ABI et de bibliothèque.

   texte (§2.1, clause 4) exige « des empreintes composées exclusivement de feuilles
   d'emplacements existants ».

3. `AllocStep` accepte une forme à plusieurs racines, alors qu'O14 crée « une nouvelle racine ».

4. `free` et `endUse` ne marquent pas morts tous les stockages possédés qui cessent de vivre :

   - `endUseS` marque morts les seuls emplacements possédés directement par `p` ou ses parties ;
     O12 marque morts « les emplacements possédés transitivement qui cessent de vivre ».

/-- Leaves that end with the value at `p` (A6): those of `p`, and those of places that stop
being usable. -/
def EndingLeaf (s : S3) (p l : Nat) : Prop :=
  l ∈ footprint s.P p ∨ (s.Usable l ∧ ¬ (endUseS s p).Usable l)

instance (s : S3) (p l : Nat) : Decidable (EndingLeaf s p l) := by
  unfold EndingLeaf; infer_instance

/-- Root of the value at `p` (A6, pass-1 arbitrage 2): an authority without origin covering a
leaf of `p`. -/
def IsRootOf (s : S3) (p : Nat) (y : Authority) : Prop :=
  y.origin = none ∧ ∃ l ∈ footprint s.P p, l ∈ y.footprint

instance (s : S3) (p : Nat) (y : Authority) : Decidable (IsRootOf s p y) := by
  unfold IsRootOf; infer_instance

/-- Authority `a` is released by the end of the value at `p` (A4, A6): it is active, and held
within `p` (released by `endUseS`) or by a holder that is not live after `endUseS` (released by
`cleanup`). Under the possession clause of `WF3`, that holder dies with `p`. -/
def EndUseReleased (s : S3) (p a : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun z => z.active = true ∧
    (heldIn s.P p z.holder ∨ ¬ HolderLive (endUseS s p) z.holder)) False

instance (s : S3) (p a : Nat) : Decidable (EndUseReleased s p a) := by
  unfold EndUseReleased; infer_instance

/-- Authority `j` does not block the end of the value at `p` (A6): if it is an active derived
authority on an ending leaf, or descending from an authority that the end releases
(MM-03.3 §3, O3.2), it is held within `p` or its holder dies. -/
def EndUseAccessOK (s : S3) (p j : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun y => y.active = true → y.origin ≠ none →
    ((∃ l ∈ y.footprint, EndingLeaf s p l) ∨ ∃ a ∈ s.ancs j, EndUseReleased s p a) →
      heldIn s.P p y.holder ∨ ¬ HolderLive (endUseS s p) y.holder) True

instance (s : S3) (p j : Nat) : Decidable (EndUseAccessOK s p j) := by
  unfold EndUseAccessOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Anchor `x` survives the end of the value at `p` (A6): not held within `p`, not the root of
`p`, with a holder that stays live. -/
def EndUseAnchorOK (s : S3) (p x : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => ¬ heldIn s.P p y.holder ∧ ¬ IsRootOf s p y ∧
    HolderLive (endUseS s p) y.holder) True

instance (s : S3) (p x : Nat) : Decidable (EndUseAnchorOK s p x) := by
  unfold EndUseAnchorOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `endUse p` (A6). Usability of the anchored places is read after the end:
a place that dies with `p` has no usable dependent afterwards. In order: `p` usable;
exercisable `Modify` on `p` (A2);
no active derived authority on an ending leaf, or descending from an authority that the end
releases (MM-03.3 §3, O3.2), held elsewhere than in `p` and staying live; no
usable place anchored on an authority held by `p`, on its root, or held by a holder that dies;
C5: no ending leaf pinned, dynamically (A8) or statically (`Pinned`), whatever `ExternalDone`
says: external obligations end only through `unpin`. The ending leaves include those of the
owned places, which die (A6). C8: `p` itself stays usable, its leaves `Uninit`. -/
def EndUsePre (k : K) (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop :=
  s.Usable p ∧ HasRight s .modify p ∧
  (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, EndUseAccessOK s p j) ∧
  (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (endUseS s p).Usable q → ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s p).D q,
    EndUseAnchorOK s p x) ∧
  (∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, EndingLeaf s p l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l)

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (p : Nat) :
    Decidable (EndUsePre k s p) := by
  unfold EndUsePre; infer_instance

/-- `endUse` as a relation (A6). -/
def EndUseStep (k : K) (p : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (EndUsePre k s p) (endUseEff s p)

/-- `NoOrphan` read with effective coverage (`CoversHolderEff`), everything else as in G3. -/
def NoOrphanEff (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : Nat) (y : Authority) (q : Nat), s.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true → y.holder = .place q →
    ∃ (a₀ : Nat) (z : Authority) (f : Nat) (c : List Nat), s.A[a₀]? = some z ∧ z.active = true ∧
      z.holder = .frame f ∧ f ∈ s.F ∧ (a₀ :: c).Nodup ∧ (a₀ :: c).getLast? = some x ∧
      Linked (CoversHolderEff s) (a₀ :: c)

theorem linked_closed {R : Nat → Nat → Prop} {S : Nat → Prop} (hR : ∀ a b, S a → R a b → S b) :
    ∀ (l : List Nat) (a : Nat), Linked R (a :: l) → S a →
      ∀ x, (a :: l).getLast? = some x → S x
  | [], a, _, ha, x, h => by
    simp only [List.getLast?_singleton, Option.some.injEq] at h; subst h; exact ha
  | b :: l, a, h, ha, x, hx =>
    linked_closed hR l b h.2 (hR a b ha h.1) x (by rw [getLast?_cons_ne (by simp)] at hx; exact hx)

/-- A list `S` of authorities that contains every active authority held by a frame of the stack
and is closed under `CoversHolderEff` refutes `NoOrphanEff` if it misses an active authority held
by a place. -/
theorem not_noOrphanEff (s : S3) (S : List Nat)
    (h0 : ∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, OptP (s.A[a]?) (fun z => z.active = true →
      OptP (holderFrame z.holder) (fun f => f ∈ s.F → a ∈ S) True) True)
    (h1 : ∀ a ∈ S, ∀ b ∈ List.range s.A.length, CoversHolderEff s a b → b ∈ S)
    (x : Nat) (y : Authority) (q : Nat) (hx : s.A[x]? = some y) (ya : y.active = true)
    (hh : y.holder = .place q) (hxS : x ∉ S) : ¬ NoOrphanEff s := by
  intro hno
  obtain ⟨a₀, z, f, c, hz, za, zh, hf, -, hlast, hlink⟩ := hno x y q hx ya hh
  have ha0 : a₀ ∈ S := by
    have := h0 a₀ (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hz))
    simp only [OptP, hz, za, zh, holderFrame, forall_const] at this
    exact this hf
  refine hxS (linked_closed (S := (· ∈ S)) (fun a b ha hab => ?_) c a₀ hlink ha0 x hlast)
  have hb : b < s.A.length := by
    unfold CoversHolderEff OptP at hab
    split at hab
    · exact lt_of_getElem? ‹_›
    · exact hab.elim
  exact h1 a ha b (List.mem_range.2 hb) hab

/-- With effective coverage, G3 would be false on reached states (G3): in `hu1` and `iu1`,
`NoOrphan` holds but `NoOrphanEff` does not. -/
theorem noOrphanEff_fails :
    Reachable K0 [] hu1 ∧ NoOrphan hu1 ∧ ¬ NoOrphanEff hu1 ∧
      Reachable K0 [] iu1 ∧ NoOrphan iu1 ∧ ¬ NoOrphanEff iu1 := by
  obtain ⟨r, -, -, -, -, -, -, hn, -⟩ := held_unexercisable_by_transfer
  obtain ⟨r', -, -, hn', -⟩ := held_unexercisable_by_issue
  exact ⟨r, hn, not_noOrphanEff hu1 [0, 1] (by decide) (by decide) 2
    ⟨.modify, some 1, [3], .place 3, true⟩ 3 (by decide) rfl rfl (by decide), r', hn',
    not_noOrphanEff iu1 [0, 1, 2, 3, 4] (by decide) (by decide) 5
    ⟨.modify, some 4, [5], .place 5, true⟩ 5 (by decide) rfl rfl (by decide)⟩

/-! ## New cases of pass 8 (J1) -/

/-- J1: the transfer of a structure whose field holds a stored authority moves that authority to the
corresponding field of the destination. In `fw3`, the view 5 is held by the field 3 of the structure
2; after the transfer of 2 into the structure 4, it is held by the field 5 of 4. -/
theorem transfer_field_authority_follows :
    TransferStep K0 2 4 fw3 (.ok (transferEff fw3 2 4)) ∧ corr fw3.P 2 4 3 = some 5 ∧
      (fw3.A[5]?).map (·.holder) = some (.place 3) ∧
      ((transferEff fw3 2 4).A[5]?).map (·.holder) = some (.place 5) :=
  ⟨.ok (by decide), by decide, by decide, by decide⟩

A feature must not be adopted solely because it is novel or exists in another language.

## 4. Memory Model and Safety

ERN aims to provide a memory model that enables precise low-level control, efficient resource management, and clearly defined safety guarantees.

### 4.1 Safety Contract

Safe ERN code must guarantee:

1. **Spatial memory safety**.
2. **Temporal memory safety**.
3. **Absence of reads of uninitialized values**.
4. **Absence of type confusion**.
5. **Absence of data races**.

These guarantees also depend on the contracts of any unsafe abstractions being respected.

The safety contract does not automatically guarantee the absence of:

- Memory or resource leaks.
- Deadlocks.
- Stack overflows.

These exclusions do not prevent the language or its libraries from providing mechanisms for prevention, detection, or diagnosis.

### 4.2 Memory Model

Rules governing values, storage locations, references, memory accesses, resources, invalidation, and unsafe operations will be established by the memory model specification.

The safety contract must distinguish guarantees applicable to safe code from the obligations associated with unsafe operations.

The charter does not presuppose any particular model of ownership, borrowing, regions, or destruction.

## 5. Concurrency and Asynchrony

## 13. Specifications and Formalization

### 13.1 Document Responsibilities

The charter establishes the objectives, principles, and design order.

Specifications establish language mechanisms, their behaviors, and their normative guarantees.

A specification may cover multiple closely related mechanisms.

No subdivision into additional documents is required unless necessary.

### 13.2 Specification Content

Each specification defines, as appropriate to its scope:

- The concepts involved.
- Semantic rules.
- Permitted and forbidden behaviors.
- Invariants.
- Examples and counterexamples.
- Stress-test cases and their expected verdicts.
- Interactions with other specifications.

### 13.3 Formalization

Lean 4 is used progressively as a tool for designing, evaluating, and verifying the semantic properties of the language.

Formal models accompany the design of mechanisms and enable examination of their guarantees before stabilization.

Validated specifications constitute the normative reference; formal models must remain consistent with their rules.

### 13.4 Syntax

Abstract syntax and provisional notations may precede the final grammar.

The normative grammar is established after the corresponding semantic mechanisms have been stabilized.

### 13.5 Sources of Truth

formal/DESIGN.md, draft `formal/derivability_0.1` files MM03.lean, Derived/Arena.lean (step_inv57,

MM03_v0.1_p8.md, MM23_v0.1.md (f), Derivability_v0.1.md, Jalon3 material §7, v0.4 Annex A and F.

All file:line references are on branch `formal/derivability_0.1` (`formal/Ern/<file>`). "MM03" =
`formal/Ern/MM03.lean`. Draft docstrings cite "MM-03.3 §n" and arbitrage codes (A1..J1), never spec
v0 sections: every reused declaration needs its citation rewritten (AGENTS: "cites the rule's location").

Lean checks written for this map (compiled with `lean` against the draft oleans in
`formal/.lake/build/lib/lean`, MM03.olean built Oct 30 18:12, last MM03.lean commit Oct 30 18:13;
nothing in the repository was modified):
- `check/Cyc.lean`: transfer creating an ownership cycle (spec problem P1);
- `check/Stat.lean`: cyclic statics (P2);
- `check/EU.lean`: endUse leaving an active authority with an inactive origin (P5);
- `check/ND.lean`: `exitFrame_no_dangling` needs I1 once `RootHeld` is the §49.7 clause.
(paths under `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/ref/map/`)

Counts (section 1): **44 SAME, 12 DIFFERS, 4 MISSING** (1 row out of scope).

---

## 1. Clause table

### 1.A §50 — I1, structural exclusivity

| Clause | Draft | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 50.a "For two active authorities **unrelated by derivation** covering the same leaf, their own modes must both be `Observe`." | `I1` MM03:1616: `∀ a b x y p, a ≠ b → A[a]=x → A[b]=y → x.active → y.active → p ∈ x.footprint → p ∈ y.footprint → a ∉ s.ancs b → b ∉ s.ancs a → x.mode = .observe ∧ y.mode = .observe` | SAME. Notes: "unrelated" is read on the current origin chain `s.ancs` (`chain`, MM03:47, follows only links to smaller indices, faithful under WF3 §49.5 ordering, which §49 last para permits); "leaf" is any member of a footprint, equal to "leaf" once §49.4 is in WF3 (see 1.G 49.4). |
| 50.b "This rule also applies to leaves identified as `SharedMutable` … creates no exception to I1." | `I1` has no SharedMutable exception; `shared_keeps_exclusivity` MM03:1766; `writeShared_preserves` MM03:3889 (A unchanged, I1 kept) | SAME |
| 50.c "Exclusivity of **effective** modes (`effective_exclusive`) is a consequence of I1 and the definition of `effective`, not the definition of I1." | `effective_exclusive` MM03:1758: `(h : I1 s) (hab : a ≠ b) (ha : effective s a p = some .modify) : effective s b p = none`; hypothesis is I1 only; `effective` MM03:683 per §43 | SAME |
| 50.d "On a leaf, two incompatible authorities cannot simultaneously possess incompatible effective rights." | `effective_compat` MM03:1731: under I1, `a ≠ b → effective s a p = some m₁ → effective s b p = some m₂ → Compat m₁ m₂` | SAME (stronger: any two distinct authorities, related or not) |
| 50.e "The only permitted independent ordinary coexistence is `Observe` / `Observe`." | `Compat` MM03:690 (`m₁ = .observe ∧ m₂ = .observe`) + `effective_compat` | SAME |

### 1.B §57 — main invariant

| Clause | Draft | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 57.a "`Inv3 = I1 ∧ I2 ∧ I3 ∧ I4 ∧ AnchorOrder ∧ NoDangling`" | `Inv3` MM03:1654 `Inv3base s ∧ AnchorOrder s ∧ NoDangling s`, `Inv3base` MM03:1643 `I1 ∧ I2 ∧ I3 ∧ I4` | SAME as a conjunction. Conjunct contents belong to §51–§54 mappers; two notes for them: `I2` MM03:1624 only asks the origin to exist (§51 "linked to a **valid** origin", see P5); `I4` MM03:1634 is the first sentence of §53 only and is true by construction (`i4_always` MM03:1667). |
| 57.b "On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees `WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan`" | `reachable_access_invariant_ext` MM03:8581: `(hdd : DDSound k) (h : Reachable k statics s) : WF3 s ∧ Inv3 s ∧ AnchorOrderHeld s ∧ NoOrphan s ∧ ∀ ar ∈ s.arenas, s.Active ar.internal → ArenaInv s ar` | DIFFERS: (1) `WF3` is the draft one (1.G: §49.3 missing, §49.4 weaker, §49.7 replaced by another clause); (2) extra `ArenaInv` conjunct and `S3.arenas`; (3) `Reachable` MM03:8343 also closes under `newArena`, `issue`, `reset` (library operations, §XIV) and under the draft `TransferPre` (draft-only guard MM03:1247, no §63.8), so the set of reached states is not the spec's; (4) `Reachable.init` requires `ShapeOK 0 (statics.map (·.1))`, a premise the spec does not state (P2). |
| 57.c "`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant." | `reachable_invariants` MM03:8381 concludes `ArenasWF s ∧ ArenasInv s`; `kstep_preserves_arenas` MM03:8147, `arena_inv_preserved` MM03:7418 inside the kernel module | DIFFERS (arena registry inside `S3`, `ArenaInv` in the kernel theorem) |
| 57.d "I5 … remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone." | No I5 clause in `Inv3`; `static_pinned_never_exits` MM03:5959 under `StaticPinnedBottom` hypothesis only | SAME |
| 57.e "Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below." | MM23 | out of scope (refinement map) |

### 1.C §59 — implicit preservation of modes and anchors

| Clause | Draft | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 59.a "Changes in effective authority are **derived** from active authorities and their origins; no `Suspended` indicator is mutated." | `Authority` MM03:223 has no suspension field; `effective` MM03:683 computed from `descModes` MM03:670 | SAME |
| 59.b "Access operations do not change an anchor without an explicitly authorized effect of transfer, `depend`, `store`, release, or reanchoring." | No theorem. Effects: `releaseEff` MM03:983 removes `a` from its holder's `D`; `transferEff` MM03:1076, `dependEff` MM03:1299, `storeEff` MM03:1322, `exitEff` MM03:1464 change `D`; `endUseS` MM03:3937 and `freeS` MM03:4101 clear `D` of `p` and its parts; `enterEff`/`allocEff` reset `D` on fresh indices only; derive/split/read/write3/writeShared/pin/unpin keep `D` | MISSING (no statement). The list conflicts with §69's effect (P4). |
| 59.c "Leaves becoming `Init` do so through a permitted write (`write3`, `writeShared`, `store`, including during a derived `issue`) or a transfer from a corresponding source leaf already `Init`" | `init_only_by_writes` MM03:8611: `(h : Step k s s') (hl : s.I l ≠ .init) (hl' : s'.I l = .init) : WrittenBy k s s' l`; `WrittenBy` MM03:8601 = write3 ∨ writeShared ∨ store into `l` ∨ **kernel `IssueAt` to `l`** ∨ transfer with `l ∈ footprint dst`, `corr s.P src dst l' = some l`, `s.I l' = .init` | DIFFERS (minor): `issue` is a kernel step (`Step.issue`) instead of `split`+`store`; `Step` contains arena steps; `WrittenBy` is existential over operations relating `s` and `s'` (not the executed operation). Content of the write/transfer disjuncts is SAME. |
| 59.d "leaves initialized in `S3.init` are declared as such." | `init_statics` MM03:8708: `(S3.init statics).I l = .init ↔ ∃ e, statics[l]? = some e ∧ e.2 = true` | SAME (stated for every index; non-leaf flags are never read) |
| 59.e (consequence required by the brief, v0.4 Annex F.5) every `Init` leaf of a reached state was declared or written | none; MM03_v0.1_p8.md (i) 9: "Ce n'est pas énoncé comme théorème"; v0.4 Annex A.3 | MISSING |

### 1.D §72 — O6 `enterFrame`

| Clause | Draft | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 72.1a "The calling frame is the current frame and is live." | `EnterPreBase` MM03:1405 `s.F ≠ []` (current = `s.top`, head) | SAME |
| 72.1b "Each parameter … is an active, derived authority held by the caller before the step" | `EnterPreBase` clause 2: `y.active = true ∧ y.holder = .frame s.top ∧ y.origin ≠ none` | SAME |
| 72.1c "the caller is **not necessarily** the frame in which the authority was first derived" | no lineage check | SAME |
| 72.2 "Modes, footprints, anchoring, and parameter-passing rules permit this change of holder; introduction of locals preserves well-formedness and the validity of their roots." | `EnterPreBase` clause 3 (parents of locals are earlier locals; a part has its parent's owner) | SAME |
| 72.3 "for each `Modify` parameter with direct origin `o`, `o` is exercisable in **no mode** … in the **resulting state**" | `ParamOriginHidden` MM03:1394 on `enterEff s ps ls`, required by `EnterPre` MM03:1422; restated by `enter_params_protected` MM03:10305 | SAME |
| 72.4 "**G4:** `AnchorOrderHeld` is checked over the complete resulting state." | `EnterPre` clause `AnchorOrderHeld (enterEff s ps ls)` | SAME |
| 72.E1 "A new child frame is pushed onto the stack" | `enterEff` MM03:1378 `F := s.nF :: s.F` | SAME |
| 72.E2 "active parameters **are yielded** to that frame, which becomes their sole holder" | `enterEff.A`: `if j ∈ ps then { y with holder := .frame s.nF }` | SAME |
| 72.E3 "local places and their root authorities are created" | `enterP` MM03:1365 with `localOwner` MM03:1358: a local with an owning element is owned by `.place o`, not by the frame | DIFFERS: §39 "Frames hold … directly local places"; v0.4 Annex F.2 "une forme de local ayant pour propriétaire un autre local n'est pas une forme de `enterFrame` admise" (planned change). |
| 72.E4 "valid anchors inherited from the caller are preserved" | `enterEff.D` unchanged below `s.P.length` | SAME |
| 72.E5 "This transfer creates no additional rights." | `enter_preserves` MM03:3197 (I1, I2 kept) | SAME |
| 72.6 "This clause establishes **entry protection**. It does not prove the stronger property … deferred to Spec 3." | `CallProtects` MM03:10238 (ghost `callParams`), `call_protects_params_safe_false` MM03:10425 refutes the stronger property on reached states | SAME (the draft claims nothing stronger; `callParams` is auxiliary data allowed by §38 and read by no operation) |
| 72.7 "While a `Modify` parameter remains active, its direct origin remains subject to effective-mode restrictions." | `call_params_effective_protected` MM03:10282 | SAME (see 3.d) |

### 1.E §73 — O7 `exitFrame` (and §39 on exited frames)

| Clause | Draft | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 73.1 "The current frame is not the initial frame and has a surviving caller." | `ExitPre` MM03:1479 `F₀ ≠ []` (base frame 0 is last: `reachable_base_owns_statics` MM03:9780) | SAME |
| 73.2 "Results that must survive have already been legally transferred …; no active authority or dependency may remain invalidly attached to locals that are about to die." | `ExitPre` clause 2 (every anchor of a place usable after exit has a surviving authority among itself and its ancestors) + effect | SAME |
| 73.3 "No leaf of a place that dies with the frame … is pinned" | `ExitPre` clause 4 (`s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l` for places usable before and not after) | SAME |
| 73.4 "Iterated reanchoring … reaches the **first surviving active origin** … not permitted to skip a surviving origin merely because it is held by a place … rejected when no suitable surviving origin exists" | `Survives` MM03:1441 (active ∧ `HolderLive { s with F := F₀ }`), `firstSurv` MM03:1448, `ExitPre` clause 3 | SAME |
| 73.5 "Validity of anchors of surviving values and `AnchorOrderHeld` are checked **in the resulting state**." | `ExitPre` clause 2 and `AnchorOrderHeld (exitEff s)` | SAME |

| 73.E2 "authorities still held by that frame, or by places that have become unusable, are released" | `exitG` MM03:1454 (`{ y with active := false }` unless `Survives`); `exitFrame_releases_all` MM03:3650 | SAME |
| 73.E3 "origins … reanchored to the **first surviving active origin** …, and the `D` anchors of surviving values are correspondingly reanchored" | `exitG` origin `firstSurv s F₀ (s.ancs a)`; `exitEff.D` `(firstSurv s F₀ (x :: s.ancs x)).getD x`; `exitFrame_reanchors_to_origin` MM03:3719 | SAME |
| 73.E4 "reanchoring changes **neither the footprint nor the own mode** …; parameter identities … cease their operational role" | `exitG` changes only `origin`/`active`; `callParams` read by no operation | SAME |
| 73.E5 "the calling frame becomes current again" | `F := F₀` | SAME |
| 73.6 "Exiting does not entail automatic physical deallocation … `defer` lies outside this kernel." | `exitEff` leaves `freed` unchanged | SAME |
| §39 "An exited frame can neither be the terminal owner of a usable place nor hold an authority that remains active." | `exitFrame_kills_owned` MM03:3701, `exitFrame_releases_all` MM03:3650 | SAME |

## 4. Spec problems

**P1 (blocking for (a)/(b)): a `transfer` accepted by §63 breaks §49.8 and `NoDangling`.**
Passages: §63 effect "places owned by `r` become owned by `corr(r)`"; §63.7 "All moved held authorities … satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state"; §44 "`AnchorOrder` requires, for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a **usable** place `q` … `AnchorOrderHeld` imposes the same rule on every active authority held by `q`"; §63.8 (local check on leaves of `corr(r)` only); §49.8 "every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place"; §49 "Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a required property of transitions"; §58 "An `ok` transition must … preserve the relevant invariants"; §40 "An ownership cycle makes no place usable."
Example (`check/Cyc.lean`, every step `ok` in the draft and reached): frame 1 with locals `src` (0) and `prov` (1); `write3 prov`; `alloc(prov, one leaf, owner = src)` gives place 2 owned by `src`, root authority 2 held by `src`; `alloc(prov, one leaf, owner = 2)` gives place 3 owned by 2, root 3 held by 2; `write3 src`; then `transfer(src, 3)`.
§63.1–§63.8 hold: both usable, exercisable `Modify` on 0 (root 0) and on 3 (root 3 via root 2 via root 0); same shape (single leaves); `src` Init, 3 Uninit, disjoint; no pins, no anchors; authority 2 (held by part `src`) moves to `corr(src) = 3` and its footprint `[2]` contains no leaf of 3 (§63.8); in the result place 3 is not usable, so `AnchorOrderHeld` is vacuous for it. Lean confirms every draft `TransferPre` clause except the draft-only `(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst` (MM03:1247).
Result: place 2 is owned by 3 and 3 by 2; authority 2 is active, held by the unusable place 3 (§49.8 false) and covers leaf 2 of the unusable place 2 (`NoDangling` false); under the global reading of §49.3 (P3) the cycle also violates WF3.3. The draft rejects the step only through its own clause, which has no spec text. Not a charter §4.1 violation (authorities 2 and 3 are no longer exercisable: `ExercisableAt` is inductive and the holder chain is cyclic; the storage leaks, which charter §4.1 permits), but the §57 guarantee is false for the spec as written. Needed decision: e.g. require the destination usable in the resulting state, or read §63.7 as requiring every moved authority's new holder to have a frame.

**P2: well-formedness of the declared statics is not stated (§47, §57).**
§47: "a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter." Nothing excludes cycles or a part owned differently from its parent. Example (`check/Stat.lean`): statics 0 owned by 1 and 1 owned by 0: in `S3.init`, authority 0 is active and held by place 1, and places 0 and 1 are unusable, so §49.8 fails in the initial state and "reachable ⇒ WF3" (§57) is false. The draft adds `ShapeOK` (owners and parents are earlier statics, a part has its parent's owner) as a premise of `Reachable.init`; it is a representation of "well-formed declaration" only if the spec says statics are well-formed.

**P3: scope of "well-founded" in §49.3.**
"valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place" reads either (A) all ownership chains are well-founded, and those of usable places reach a live frame, or (B) for every usable place, its chain is well-founded and reaches a live frame. Under (B) the clause is implied by the inductive `Usable` and adds nothing; under (A) the state `DraftGaps.wf_cyc` (MM23.lean:3899, two places owning each other, no authority) violates WF3. v0.4 FR "des chaînes de possession bien fondées, qui atteignent un cadre vivant pour chaque emplacement utilisable" leans to (A); MM23_v0.1.md (f) 6 used (A). The planned "WF3 gains well-founded ownership" presupposes (A). Under (A), P1 also breaks WF3.3.

**P4: §59.b anchor list vs §69 effect.**
§59: "Access operations do not change an anchor without an explicitly authorized effect of transfer, `depend`, `store`, release, or reanchoring." §69 effect: "dependencies of the ended value are removed" while "`place` **remains usable as a place**". Example: `store a p` gives `D(p) = [a]`; `endUse p` makes `D(p) = []` with `p` usable (draft `endUseS` MM03:3937 does this). If "access operations" means all kernel operations, §59 forbids what §69 prescribes (endUse is not in the list; nor is the clearing of `D` by `free`, draft `freeS` MM03:4101, which §70 does not state). If it means O9–O11 only, there is no conflict. The statement of a §59 anchor theorem depends on the reading.

**P5: "valid origin" in §51 is undefined, and decides whether `endUse` preserves I2.**
§51: "Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules." §44 defines validity for anchors only ("valid as long as the authority it names is active"). Example (`check/EU.lean`, reached): frame 1 locals X (0, Init) and p (1); derive 2 from root 0 on X (`Modify`); `store 2 p`; derive 3 from 2 on X (held by frame 1). `endUse p`: §69.2 concerns descendants "over the leaves of `place` or storage that dies with it" (3 covers X, which does not die), §69.3 holds once `p`'s dependencies are removed, §69.4 no pins; so the spec accepts it, and the effect releases 2 (held by `p`) while 3 stays active with origin 2 inactive. If "valid origin" means active, I2 fails after an accepted step; if it means existing, I2 holds, and the draft's extra `EndUseAccessOK` disjunct "`∃ a ∈ s.ancs j, EndUseReleased s p a`" (MM03:3979), which rejects this step (Lean confirms the rejection comes from that disjunct only), has no spec text. Primarily for the §51/§69 maps; it decides the endUse case of (a).

**P6 (silence): the footprint of a root authority is never stated.**
§40 "Every root place has a root authority of own mode `Modify`, with no origin, held exactly by that place's owner"; §47, §49.6–7, §71, §72 never say it covers `footprint(r)`. The draft fixes `footprint (P) r` (`S3.init`, `enterEff`, `allocEff`, `RootLive`, `RootChain`). A smaller footprint would change accepted programs (`HasRight` on fresh storage fails) and makes `NoOrphan` underivable from `WF3` (`chain_to_frame` uses `z.footprint = footprint r`). The natural reading is `footprint(r)`; it needs confirmation, not a choice.

No contradiction with the charter found in this scope (P1 produces a leak and broken invariants, not an exercisable access).

1. `Reachable` as the closure of one `Step` relation (`init` + `step`), `Step` = the ok-outcomes of O1–O16; `read` keeps the state. Makes (i) definitional.

## 4. Spec problems

**P1 (blocking for (a)/(b)): a `transfer` accepted by §63 breaks §49.8 and `NoDangling`.**
Passages: §63 effect "places owned by `r` become owned by `corr(r)`"; §63.7 "All moved held authorities … satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state"; §44 "`AnchorOrder` requires, for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a **usable** place `q` … `AnchorOrderHeld` imposes the same rule on every active authority held by `q`"; §63.8 (local check on leaves of `corr(r)` only); §49.8 "every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place"; §49 "Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a required property of transitions"; §58 "An `ok` transition must … preserve the relevant invariants"; §40 "An ownership cycle makes no place usable."
Example (`check/Cyc.lean`, every step `ok` in the draft and reached): frame 1 with locals `src` (0) and `prov` (1); `write3 prov`; `alloc(prov, one leaf, owner = src)` gives place 2 owned by `src`, root authority 2 held by `src`; `alloc(prov, one leaf, owner = 2)` gives place 3 owned by 2, root 3 held by 2; `write3 src`; then `transfer(src, 3)`.
§63.1–§63.8 hold: both usable, exercisable `Modify` on 0 (root 0) and on 3 (root 3 via root 2 via root 0); same shape (single leaves); `src` Init, 3 Uninit, disjoint; no pins, no anchors; authority 2 (held by part `src`) moves to `corr(src) = 3` and its footprint `[2]` contains no leaf of 3 (§63.8); in the result place 3 is not usable, so `AnchorOrderHeld` is vacuous for it. Lean confirms every draft `TransferPre` clause except the draft-only `(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst` (MM03:1247).
Result: place 2 is owned by 3 and 3 by 2; authority 2 is active, held by the unusable place 3 (§49.8 false) and covers leaf 2 of the unusable place 2 (`NoDangling` false); under the global reading of §49.3 (P3) the cycle also violates WF3.3. The draft rejects the step only through its own clause, which has no spec text. Not a charter §4.1 violation (authorities 2 and 3 are no longer exercisable: `ExercisableAt` is inductive and the holder chain is cyclic; the storage leaks, which charter §4.1 permits), but the §57 guarantee is false for the spec as written. Needed decision: e.g. require the destination usable in the resulting state, or read §63.7 as requiring every moved authority's new holder to have a frame.

**P2: well-formedness of the declared statics is not stated (§47, §57).**
§47: "a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter." Nothing excludes cycles or a part owned differently from its parent. Example (`check/Stat.lean`): statics 0 owned by 1 and 1 owned by 0: in `S3.init`, authority 0 is active and held by place 1, and places 0 and 1 are unusable, so §49.8 fails in the initial state and "reachable ⇒ WF3" (§57) is false. The draft adds `ShapeOK` (owners and parents are earlier statics, a part has its parent's owner) as a premise of `Reachable.init`; it is a representation of "well-formed declaration" only if the spec says statics are well-formed.

**P3: scope of "well-founded" in §49.3.**
"valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place" reads either (A) all ownership chains are well-founded, and those of usable places reach a live frame, or (B) for every usable place, its chain is well-founded and reaches a live frame. Under (B) the clause is implied by the inductive `Usable` and adds nothing; under (A) the state `DraftGaps.wf_cyc` (MM23.lean:3899, two places owning each other, no authority) violates WF3. v0.4 FR "des chaînes de possession bien fondées, qui atteignent un cadre vivant pour chaque emplacement utilisable" leans to (A); MM23_v0.1.md (f) 6 used (A). The planned "WF3 gains well-founded ownership" presupposes (A). Under (A), P1 also breaks WF3.3.

**P4: §59.b anchor list vs §69 effect.**
§59: "Access operations do not change an anchor without an explicitly authorized effect of transfer, `depend`, `store`, release, or reanchoring." §69 effect: "dependencies of the ended value are removed" while "`place` **remains usable as a place**". Example: `store a p` gives `D(p) = [a]`; `endUse p` makes `D(p) = []` with `p` usable (draft `endUseS` MM03:3937 does this). If "access operations" means all kernel operations, §59 forbids what §69 prescribes (endUse is not in the list; nor is the clearing of `D` by `free`, draft `freeS` MM03:4101, which §70 does not state). If it means O9–O11 only, there is no conflict. The statement of a §59 anchor theorem depends on the reading.

**P5: "valid origin" in §51 is undefined, and decides whether `endUse` preserves I2.**
§51: "Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules." §44 defines validity for anchors only ("valid as long as the authority it names is active"). Example (`check/EU.lean`, reached): frame 1 locals X (0, Init) and p (1); derive 2 from root 0 on X (`Modify`); `store 2 p`; derive 3 from 2 on X (held by frame 1). `endUse p`: §69.2 concerns descendants "over the leaves of `place` or storage that dies with it" (3 covers X, which does not die), §69.3 holds once `p`'s dependencies are removed, §69.4 no pins; so the spec accepts it, and the effect releases 2 (held by `p`) while 3 stays active with origin 2 inactive. If "valid origin" means active, I2 fails after an accepted step; if it means existing, I2 holds, and the draft's extra `EndUseAccessOK` disjunct "`∃ a ∈ s.ancs j, EndUseReleased s p a`" (MM03:3979), which rejects this step (Lean confirms the rejection comes from that disjunct only), has no spec text. Primarily for the §51/§69 maps; it decides the endUse case of (a).

**P6 (silence): the footprint of a root authority is never stated.**
§40 "Every root place has a root authority of own mode `Modify`, with no origin, held exactly by that place's owner"; §47, §49.6–7, §71, §72 never say it covers `footprint(r)`. The draft fixes `footprint (P) r` (`S3.init`, `enterEff`, `allocEff`, `RootLive`, `RootChain`). A smaller footprint would change accepted programs (`HasRight` on fresh storage fails) and makes `NoOrphan` underivable from `WF3` (`chain_to_frame` uses `z.footprint = footprint r`). The natural reading is `footprint(r)`; it needs confirmation, not a choice.

No contradiction with the charter found in this scope (P1 produces a leak and broken invariants, not an exercisable access).

---

## 5. Representation choices (no accepted program changes)

1. `Reachable` as the closure of one `Step` relation (`init` + `step`), `Step` = the ok-outcomes of O1–O16; `read` keeps the state. Makes (i) definitional.
2. Labelled steps: `inductive Op` (as HandlePool.lean:1535) and `OpStep k : Op → S3 → Outcome → Prop`, `Step k s s' := ∃ o, OpStep k o s (.ok s')`; `WrittenBy` keyed on the executed `o`; executions as lists of `(Op, S3)` for (h).
3. `WF3`, `Inv3`, and every operation precondition as `structure`s with named fields citing §49.n / §6x.n, replacing positional `∧` chains (`hpre.2.2.2…`), so that adding §63.8 or §49 clauses does not break unrelated proofs.
4. Keep index ordering for acyclicity of origins (`a < b`) and composition (`r < q`) (§49 last para).
5. §49.3 as `∀ q < s.P.length, ∃ f, FrameOf s q f` (inductive, so finite chains) once P3 is settled; §49.4 as `FpLeaves`; §49.7 as `RootLive` with `z.mode = .modify`.
6. Fresh locals and fresh allocation leaves start `Uninit` (§71 explicit; for §72, forced by §59 and §41 "`Moved`: value consumed by transfer").
7. Keep `nF` (fresh frame identities), `dead`, `freed`, `pin` as auxiliary state (§38 "auxiliary information that creates no new rights").
8. `effective_exclusive`, `effective_compat`, `call_params_effective_protected` stay stated on arbitrary states under I1 alone.
9. Statics as a well-formed shape list with Boolean init flags (draft `Statics` MM03:5461), pending P2.

4. **`exitFrame_no_dangling` (MM03:5715) depends on the draft `RootHeld`.** Under spec `WF3` it is false without I1 (`ND.lean`). It must be restated under `WF3 ∧ Inv3` and reproved, together with `exit_preserves_noDangling`, `endUse_preserves_noDangling` and `free_preserves_noDangling`.

The result is an ownership cycle with an active authority held by an unusable place. - **P5.** "Valid origin" in §51 is undefined. A spec-accepted `endUse` leaves an active authority whose origin is inactive. The draft prevents this with an extra `EndUseAccessOK` disjunct (MM03:3979) that has no spec text.
